title: Cosmos DB: partition key, and the design that decides everything after

videos.script: Quitanda's app shows a customer their orders, all day, in a few milliseconds. On Azure that is Cosmos DB's job. {{app}} Cosmos DB stores JSON items in containers. Every container is created with a partition key, a path into each item, and it can never change. {{key}} Every item with the same value lives together, in one logical partition. Azure hashes those onto physical partitions, and splits them as the data grows. {{partitions}} So the key decides what a read costs. A point read names the key. A query that does not name it asks every partition. {{reads}} The emulator charges one request unit for everything, and has one physical partition, so it cannot show you that. This lesson says where it stops. {{emulator}} Then you measure four candidate keys over a year of orders. One spreads perfectly and answers nothing. One puts the whole evening on one partition. {{measure}} And for the customer who outgrows a single partition, a key with more than one level. {{hierarchy}}
